title: Postman Pricing 2026: Free, Team and Enterprise Plans
summary: Postman pricing offers a free plan for one developer and team tiers starting at $19 per user monthly, scaling as you add members.
body_markdown:
## When Postman is the wrong tool and Activepieces fits


If the job is running API calls on a schedule or in response to events across your business apps, you need a workflow tool.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) is built for that, and its free plan includes unlimited flows, 1,000 credits a month and up to 5 users. Staying free on Postman leaves you managing conflicts and access by hand.


Paying for more seats to fix that is the wrong purchase if the real task was never testing in the first place.


### Scheduled and event-driven API calls


Built for a person sitting at a screen, Postman is where you send a request, read the response, document how the API behaves, and share that with teammates.


Not all small-team work is that. It's "every morning, pull yesterday's orders," or "when a customer fills in this form, create a record in the CRM and tell the sales channel in Slack." Nobody is sitting there pressing send.


That's the gap. Jobs that point away from Postman look like this:


- Run an API call on a schedule
- Trigger a call when something happens in an app
- Chain calls across several business apps, passing results along
- Retry a call that failed
- Route the result to Slack or a spreadsheet


In each item, the cost of doing nothing is a person doing it by hand, or a script nobody owns. A tool that runs unattended removes that person from the loop.


Paying for Postman seats to cover this work buys you a tool that tests the calls well but never runs them for you.


### How per-seat pricing limits automation


Activepieces starts a flow from a trigger, either a schedule or an event in an app, and then runs steps that call other apps or any API you point it at.


**Per-seat pricing rations automation** , because every new person is a line item and IT hands out licences to a chosen few.


**Activepieces meters by credits that follow usage** , with unlimited flows on every plan, the free one included, so a colleague you add costs nothing until their flows run.


Each team works in its own project, connecting only the apps an admin has allowed, with credentials held centrally rather than in individual logins. Alan and Funding Societies run production automation on it, and the credit-based structure is laid out on the Activepieces pricing page.


I haven't checked its pricing page against today's date for this integration, so check the current plans and run limits there before you commit. Task quotas, not seats, are the thing to price.


It doesn't replace Postman's job. It won't give you a place to explore an unfamiliar API, write test suites for it, or publish documentation for other developers.


A small team that needs both can use Postman to work out how a call behaves, then Activepieces to run that call on a timetable, where a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has.
